case.pattern_description: The transaction was an online card-not-present purchase originating from a new device where the customer explicitly denied making the purchase during validation.
case.summary: Case HHG-019 concluded with a fraud verdict and resulted in a $99.92 financial exposure due to an unauthorized card-not-present transaction from a new device. Although the device fingerprint was shared across multiple cards and initially flagged with a 0.95 fraud probability, the case was automatically escalated for review. The customer confirmed they did not make the purchase and still possessed the physical card, which triggered an L1 card block and finalized the fraud determination.

evidence.claim: Card ID resolved from case hint
Checked for similar past closed cases (0 found)
Device profile found for flagged transaction
Device profile shared by 10 cards — treated as a generic OS/browser/screen fingerprint, not a ring signal
Case written to graph as CASE-HHG-019

sar.reason: No FILE_REPORT criteria met: exposure $99.92 does not exceed the $1,000 R2 threshold; no shared-device link was found (R6); pattern was not classified as undocumented (R9).

initial.reason: R1 (extended): fraud probability 0.95 is high, but rests on a single signal with no external corroboration; verify before blocking per the policy's stated intent not to block a legitimate customer

next_best_actions.what_changed: Customer denial raised the case from probability 0.95 to a confirmed fraud verdict.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: Customer states they did not make this purchase and still has the card
